diagnosis: All four rollouts exhibited the same pattern: every private fact (PF1–PF4) was successfully revealed by its owner and cited in justification_fact_ids, but the content checks failed because the settlements encoded the *wrong values* for key fields. The decisive_facts specify that PF1 changes session length from 15 minutes to 20 minutes (C2), and requires a technical-operations commitment (C7); PF2 requires a rights-compliance commitment (C8); PF3 requires citing Sofia's finding plus an accessibility commitment (C9); PF4 requires a creator-appearance commitment (C10). In every rollout, session_minutes stayed 15 (the draft default) instead of becoming 20, and the commitments were generic document_update/operational_adjustment entries rather than the specific commitment types the checks expect. C1 and C2 both failed because the settlement never set session_minutes to 20 — the model treated the 15-minute draft value as final rather than applying PF1's flip. C6 failed because the settlement contained no creator-appearance-specific commitment. C7 failed because no technical-operations commitment was present. C8 failed because no rights-compliance commitment appeared. C9 failed because no accessibility-specific commitment was present. C10 failed for the same creator-appearance-commitment reason. Only C3 (station_count=6) and C4 (public_showings=3, visitor_recording_permitted=false) passed, and P1 passed in all rollouts. The root cause is ENCODING MISMATCH: the facts were revealed and cited, but the settlement decisions and commitment structures did not match the field names, values, or commitment types the checks are looking for — most critically, no rollout applied the 15→20 minute session-length flip from PF1.
